comparisons.peer_summary: Total Intel Products revenue was $48.9 billion in 2024, an increase of $1.3 billion from 2023, driven by growth in both Client Computing Group (CCG) and Data Center and AI (DCAI) segments.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Intel disclose specific performance drivers for their client-side processor revenues, highlighting the interplay between shipment volumes and average selling prices (ASPs). AMD reported a 52% increase in Client net revenue driven by a 34% rise in unit shipments and a 13% increase in ASPs due to Ryzen processors. Intel similarly detailed its Client Computing Group (CCG) performance, noting that Notebook revenue increased $1.0 billion driven by a 12% volume increase, while ASPs remained flat, and Desktop revenue declined as volumes decreased. Both disclosures use volume and ASP changes to explain revenue movements in the client PC market.

sentences.text: Client net revenue of $7.1 billion in 2024 increased by 52%, compared to net revenue of $4.7 billion in 2023, primarily due to a 34% increase in unit shipments and a 13% increase in average selling price driven by strong demand for AMD mobile and desktop Ryzen processors.

▪CCG revenue increased $1.0 billion from 2023. Notebook revenue was $19.1 billion in 2024, up $2.1 billion from 2023. Notebook volume increased 12% from 2023, as customer inventory levels improved compared to higher levels in 2023. Notebook ASPs were roughly flat with 2023. Desktop revenue was $9.7 billion, down $516 million from 2023. Desktop volume decreased 5% from 2023, primarily due to lower demand compared to 2023. Desktop ASPs were roughly flat with 2023. Other CCG revenue was $1.6 billion, down $530 million from 2023, primarily driven by the exit of legacy businesses.

peer_results.rationale: Micron's disclosures relate to memory products (DRAM and NAND) and bit shipments, which are upstream components or distinct from AMD's logic/client processor segment. While both are semiconductors, the specific business drivers (bit volume vs. CPU unit shipments) and product categories (memory vs. client computing) are not substantively comparable for the same topic.

NVIDIA's disclosures focus on Data Center, Compute, and Networking revenue drivers, specifically AI accelerators and GPUs. This is a different market segment (data center/AI) compared to AMD's Client segment (PC processors), making the drivers and revenue streams non-comparable.

Qualcomm's disclosures focus on consolidated financial results and QTL (licensing) revenue drivers related to 3G/4G/5G products. This does not align with the specific client PC processor revenue and volume/ASP drivers disclosed by AMD.
